saml.description: When SAML username mapping is absent or empty, Casdoor derives the username from email first and falls back to NameID only if email is unavailable.
saml.note: Email-based account linking or collisions can be by design under this fallback and should not be flagged unless the test controls for it.

saml.description: Shared applications use organization-specific client identifiers by appending -org-<organizationName> to the client ID or application name.
saml.note: Different org-specific identifiers for the same shared app are expected and should not be treated as identity confusion.

saml.description: Email addresses are normalized to lowercase for uniqueness and duplicate checking.
saml.note: Case-only email differences are not distinct identities in Casdoor.

saml.description: Automatic account linking can match existing users by username case-insensitively.
saml.note: An external login may merge into an existing account by design rather than create a new principal.

saml.description: SAML providers always appear as buttons on the login page and require explicit user selection; Casdoor does not auto-redirect to the sole SAML provider.
saml.note: Lack of automatic redirect is expected behavior, not a broken auth flow.

saml.description: SSO logout without logoutAll=false logs the user out from all sessions and expires all tokens across applications by default.
saml.note: A logout affecting other sessions is by design and should not be mistaken for session confusion.

saml.description: When exclusive sign-in is enabled on an application, a new login deletes all previous sessions for that user and application.
saml.note: Termination of earlier sessions after a new login is expected and not a replay or session-fixation bug.

saml.description: Casdoor always signs the SAML response envelope, but assertion-level signatures are optional and controlled by application setting.
saml.note: Envelope-signed but assertion-unsigned responses may be emitted intentionally for compatibility.

saml.description: Application tag restrictions do not apply to admins and global admins.
saml.note: Admin access despite non-matching tags is expected and should not be flagged as authorization escalation.

saml.description: SSO logout defaults to full logout of all sessions and tokens when logoutAll is omitted.
saml.note: Calling logout without logoutAll=false invalidates all sessions by design.

saml.constraint: For SAML upstream login into Casdoor as SP, the Assertion Consumer Service endpoint is /api/acs and it accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST send SAMLResponse via HTTP POST binding; GET-based callbacks are invalid for Casdoor SP tests.

saml.constraint: Casdoor SAML SP tests MUST configure the external IdP with ACS URL and SP Entity ID both equal to https://<casdoor-domain>/api/acs. Using a different entity ID or ACS URL is a setup error, not a security finding.

For I1 SAML signature tests, Casdoor documentation states /api/acs only accepts POST and upstream IdPs are configured with signed documents while assertion signing may be off. The fuzzer MUST distinguish response-envelope signatures from assertion signatures when testing saml_unsigned_assertion and saml_spurious_signature; acceptance of response-signed but assertion-unsigned input may reflect IdP compatibility settings rather than total absence of signature handling unless assertion-signature requirements are explicitly established in the upstream IdP/SP pair.

For I4 SAML identity-binding tests, Casdoor's username fallback order is: configured username mapping, else email, else NameID. Therefore the fuzzer MUST control both email and NameID when testing collisions. A collision on email may be by design if username mapping is absent and email is present; a collision on NameID may occur only when email is absent.

For I4 multi-identity tests against Casdoor SAML SP, do NOT assume NameID is always the bound principal. Documentation says if username mapping is empty, Casdoor first uses email as username and only falls back to NameID when email is unavailable. Tests like saml_email_binding_collision MUST explicitly set conflicting email values because email-based linking is a documented fallback path.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, Casdoor supports MFA as a second factor on login and SAML as an alternate upstream sign-in method. A valid bypass test MUST compare the same user under password login with MFA enabled versus SAML login through an attached SAML provider. Do not treat successful SAML login as a bug unless password login for that same user/application actually triggers MFA challenge first.

Casdoor OAuth token lifetimes use sentinel semantics on application settings: RefreshExpireInHours default is 0 hours, and application config states Code resend timeout 0 means use the global default. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret 0 as immediate expiry for these fields. Specifically, code resend timeout 0 selects the global default, while refresh token expiration default 0 hours is a platform default setting rather than evidence of instant invalidation.

For I5 audience-binding tests on OAuth tokens issued after SAML login, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. The resource parameter MUST match exactly between the authorization request and token request; otherwise audience results are invalid test setup. To test wrong-audience handling, vary resource deliberately and compare against a control flow with matching resource on both requests.

For I2 freshness tests involving expired or future tokens after SAML login, include a control authorization-code exchange using a valid login flow first. Without a successful control flow, token rejection cannot be distinguished from broken application/provider setup.

Casdoor SAML providers are attached to applications and SAML login is initiated from the login page by clicking the provider button; SAML providers do not auto-redirect even when they are the only provider. The fuzzer MUST model an explicit login initiation step and MUST NOT treat absence of automatic redirect as a flow-coherence bug.

Casdoor is multi-tenant and owner semantics matter: users belong to an organization, while built-in/global admin resources are under built-in/admin. For SAML setup, applications and providers are attached within an organization/application context. The fuzzer MUST keep organization ownership consistent across created users, applications, and providers or login/setup failures will be false positives.

Application token lifetime fields use sentinel defaults: access token ExpireInHours=0 means use the platform default rather than literal zero lifetime, and refresh token RefreshExpireInHours=0 means refresh tokens are disabled by default ('default 0 hours'). Never assume 0 means immediate expiry for access tokens or unlimited refresh for refresh tokens.
Application CodeResendTimeout uses sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the global default countdown rather than literal zero seconds. Do not use 0 when testing resend timing behavior.

For I2 token-freshness tests against Casdoor OAuth/OIDC tokens, include a CONTROL login using a valid token flow alongside the attack case. A failed attack login alone cannot distinguish expiry enforcement from broken application/provider configuration.

Casdoor SAML ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. Any SAML provider used for Casdoor-as-SP testing must be configured for HTTP POST binding; redirect/GET binding to /api/acs will fail by design.

For I1 SAML signature tests against Casdoor as SP, provider trust is configured from provider metadata/parsed certificate fields (Metadata, Endpoint, IdP, Issuer URL). The fuzzer must create the SAML provider with explicit metadata and then mutate only the incoming assertion/response. If provider metadata is absent or malformed, failures are setup errors, not proof-integrity enforcement.

Casdoor username mapping for SAML has fallback semantics: if the IdP does not provide an explicit username mapping or the username field is empty, Casdoor first uses email as username, then falls back to NameID. For I4 multi-identity tests, do not assume NameID is always the binding key; vary email and NameID independently and inspect which field actually determined the resulting account.

Casdoor supports automatic account linking for external providers by OAuth identity, email/phone (if enabled), or username (case-insensitive). For SAML identity-collision tests, pre-existing users with matching email or username may be linked by design. To test principal binding correctly, control email/username values and application setting EnableLinkWithEmail before concluding an I4 violation.

Casdoor can lowercase usernames when backend config isUsernameLowered=true. Case-only differences may collapse by design. For I4 case_confusion tests, first determine whether username lowercasing is enabled; if so, 'Admin' vs 'admin' collisions are expected behavior, not necessarily a vulnerability.

Email addresses are automatically normalized to lowercase for uniqueness. For I4 tests involving email-based linking or SAML email attributes, case-only email differences must not be treated as distinct principals.

Application tags restrict sign-in by intersection with user tags, but admins and global admins are exempt. For I5 authorization-binding tests using tag restrictions, do not use admin accounts as subjects because bypass is by design.

Shared applications alter tenant binding by appending '-org-<organizationName>' to client_id or application name. For cross-org and audience-binding tests, use the organization-suffixed client_id when targeting shared applications; otherwise failures or unexpected acceptance may reflect shared-app routing semantics rather than audience validation bugs.

Exclusive sign-in is a by-design session invalidation feature: a new sign-in deletes prior sessions for that user and application. For I3 flow-coherence or I2 replay tests, disable EnableExclusiveSignin unless the test explicitly targets session replacement, or earlier sessions/tokens may be invalidated for non-security reasons.

Casdoor SAML IdP can send SAMLResponse by POST when Reply URL is set, or by GET when Reply URL is empty. For proof and audience tests involving Casdoor as IdP, set Reply URL explicitly to force POST and avoid binding-dependent behavior. For Casdoor as SP, /api/acs still accepts POST only.

Casdoor SAML assertion-signature behavior is configurable per application: responses are always signed, but assertion-level signatures can be disabled with EnableSamlAssertionSignature=false. For I1 tests such as unsigned-assertion or envelope-only signature acceptance, record this setting and distinguish compatibility mode from verifier weakness.

When testing SAML MFA bypass via alternate binding path, MFA may be configured on the user and/or via application providers/rules. A valid test must first confirm the same user is challenged under password login, then compare SAML login for that same application and user. Otherwise missing MFA may simply mean MFA was never enabled for that path.

Resource Indicator support requires exact match of the resource parameter between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. For audience-binding tests on exchanged tokens, if resource differs between the two requests, rejection is expected setup failure rather than audience enforcement on the resulting token.

Token introspection at /api/login/oauth/introspect is protected by HTTP Basic authentication using client_id:client_secret, not bearer token auth. A 401 from introspection without Basic auth is not evidence that the token is invalid.

Casdoor userinfo returns claims according to granted scope. Missing email/profile fields in /api/userinfo are by design when those scopes were not requested. For I4/I5 verification, request the necessary scopes during authorization before treating absent fields as identity loss or authorization narrowing.

Casdoor as SAML SP consumes SAML assertions only at POST /api/acs. The fuzzer MUST use HTTP POST binding for all SAML login attempts; GET/Redirect binding to /api/acs is not accepted and will fail for non-security reasons.

saml.constraint: For SAML login tests, Casdoor is SP-initiated from the login page and SAML providers always show a button instead of auto-redirecting. The fuzzer MUST initiate the login flow first and then post the forged SAMLResponse to the ACS with matching flow state; sending an unsolicited fabricated response without initiating the flow can be rejected for missing request context.

Casdoor's /api/acs endpoint only accepts POST, but when Casdoor acts as a SAML IdP its own application setting may emit GET or POST SAMLResponse depending on Reply URL. Do NOT confuse these roles: for target protocol saml against Casdoor as SP, only POST to /api/acs is valid.

For I4 SAML principal-binding tests, Casdoor's username mapping has fallback semantics: if the SAML provider does not explicitly provide a username mapping or the username field is empty, Casdoor first uses email as username and then falls back to NameID. The fuzzer MUST account for this when crafting collision tests; email-vs-NameID precedence can cause by-design merges or separations.

For I4 email-binding and account-linking tests, Casdoor supports automatic account linking by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. The fuzzer MUST distinguish documented auto-linking behavior from unintended identity collapse, especially when the same email or case-variant username is reused.

For I4 case-confusion tests, Casdoor documentation states username-based automatic account linking is case-insensitive. The fuzzer MUST treat Admin vs admin merges as potentially by-design when username linking is enabled, not automatically as a collision bug.

For I4 username normalization tests, the backend config parameter isUsernameLowered controls whether usernames are converted to lowercase. If enabled in the deployment, case-distinct test identities will normalize to the same username by design. The fuzzer MUST record this environment setting before flagging case-based collisions.

For I1 SAML signature-integrity tests such as saml_cert_substitution and saml_spurious_signature, Casdoor documentation for upstream IdP setup commonly recommends Sign Documents on and Sign Assertions off in Keycloak examples. The fuzzer MUST test both response-envelope-only signatures and assertion-level signature absence because Casdoor integrations explicitly interoperate with response-signed/assertion-unsigned IdPs.

For I1/I5 SAML audience and conditions tests, Casdoor SP Entity ID and ACS URL are both https://<casdoor-domain>/api/acs in documented setups. The fuzzer MUST use that exact SP identifier as the expected audience when crafting valid controls; mismatching audience to some other app URL will fail due to setup error, not necessarily due to security enforcement.

For I2 SAML freshness tests (expired assertion, replay), include a control login through the same provider configuration before the attack case. Otherwise a failed forged assertion cannot be distinguished from broken provider setup or missing application/provider attachment.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; it selects the platform default countdown instead.

Numeric sentinel: application CookieExpireInHours uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use default' rather than immediate expiry. Documentation also states sessions without Remember Me are limited to 24 hours regardless of the configured cookie lifetime. The fuzzer MUST not interpret 0 as zero-hour expiry.

Numeric sentinel: application quotas use -1 to mean unlimited, not a negative literal count. Tests that create organizations, users, applications, or providers must treat -1 as 'no quota limit' and not as invalid configuration.

For I3 config-change sequences, Casdoor application/provider changes are expected to affect NEW logins. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of the same authentication attempt before and after the change, not treat an admin configuration update itself as a bug.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-SAML tests, MFA is enforced as an application/user sign-in feature, while SAML upstream login is an alternate provider path. The fuzzer MUST first establish a control that password login for the same user triggers MFA, then test the SAML path for the same application and identity; otherwise success/failure is uninterpretable.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, Casdoor documentation says requested scope should be a subset of the original token's scope and omitted scope inherits the subject token scope. The fuzzer MUST compare exchanged-token scope/claims against the original authorization and treat inherited scope on omitted scope as by-design.

For I5 audience-binding tests on OAuth tokens obtained after SAML-brokered login, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. If resource is supplied at authorization time, the same exact resource value MUST also be supplied at token exchange time or the request is invalid for setup reasons. The resulting access token aud becomes the resource URI instead of the client_id.

For I5 access-control tests using application tags, only users with at least one matching tag may sign in, but admins and global admins are exempt. The fuzzer MUST avoid using admin identities when testing tag-based authorization boundaries because admin bypass is by design.

For I2 session-freshness tests, exclusive sign-in is a documented feature that invalidates prior sessions when a new login occurs for the same user and application. If enabled, a second control login will revoke the first token/session by design; do not misclassify subsequent failures of the first session as replay protection bugs.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code','urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise. MULTI-APP SEQUENCES: When a test needs two separate applications (e.g., token exchange between different clients/audiences), use 'app-test' as the SOURCE application (already exists) and create ONE new application as the TARGET. Create users with signupApplication matching the app they will login to. For login_with_password, the executor auto-resolves client_id from the user's signupApplication — so set signupApplication correctly in create_user.
